title: RAD/Paired-end RAD-Seq/ddRAD-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic for RAD/paired-end RAD/ddRAD, with the explicitly labeled fragmentation alternatives and amplified genomic DNA endpoint. Baird RAD is resolved using the supplied full-text Figure 1 and Results; Willing paired-end readout is supported at abstract level, while variant-specific paired-end and ddRAD preparation details remain qualified. The diagram has one linear panel sequence with a parenthetical ddRAD alternative, not drawn parallel experiments. Graph branching expresses that label only. Barcoded end-bearing fragments are the retained class. Optional pooling and unshown routine execution details are not added as operations. Neither catalogue modification dates nor publication metadata establish invention, equivalence, or historical development.

evidence.quote: DNA was then ligated to a second adapter (P2), a Y adapter [14] that has divergent ends (Fig. 1C). The reverse amplification primer is unable to bind to P2 unless the complementary sequence is filled in during the first round of forward elongation originating from the P1 amplification primer. states.label: Amplified restriction-site-associated genomic DNA library
features: The terminal icon is a stack of plain blue DNA lines; colored adapter marks are omitted there.
For Baird RAD this is an enriched library of P1-bearing RAD tags, with barcode-linked genomic inserts and adapter-derived sequencing interfaces; the final icon does not establish adapter removal.
The biological target and sequenced insert are genomic DNA. The library represents a reduced subset of DNA adjacent to sampled restriction sites, rather than complete uniform genomic coverage.

Sequencing this library supports SNP discovery and genotyping, with sample identity supplied by the barcode. The diagram ends at the amplified DNA product; sequencing and genotype-calling operations are described in text rather than drawn.

operations.label: Restriction digestion
operations.description: Cuts starting genomic DNA at restriction sites to create genomic fragments with restriction-generated ends. The left Genome and Restriction sites icons identify the substrate and cut positions.
operations.mechanism: Restriction-enzyme cleavage. Baird RAD explicitly reports overhanging fragment ends for subsequent P1 ligation; the schematic does not name an enzyme.
operations.information_effect: Defines the genomic anchor sites from which the reduced-representation library is drawn. Restriction-site adjacency is retained in the genomic insert.

operations.label: Add barcoded adapters
operations.description: Attaches the first barcoded adapter segments to restriction fragments, producing the long doubly end-marked fragments shown before fragmentation. In Baird RAD these are P1 adapters ligated to restriction-generated ends.

Differently colored adapter blocks illustrate different barcodes. The later barcode-to-insert association permits sample tracking.

operations.label: Shear
operations.description: For the shearing route, converts the long adapter-bearing DNA fragments into shorter fragments. The retained class shown has one barcoded restriction-associated end and a newly generated opposite end. This route is the RAD-family interpretation of the unparenthesized Shear label.
operations.mechanism: Random shearing is explicitly reported for Baird RAD. Baird also reports size selection at this boundary; no separate size-selection block or its execution settings are drawn or added to the graph.
operations.information_effect: Retains the barcode and the genomic sequence adjacent to the original restriction cut on the depicted end-bearing fragments, while creating variable opposite-end positions. This does not imply that all shearing products retain a barcode.

operations.label: Second restriction digest in ddRADseq
operations.description: Records the explicitly named ddRADseq alternative at the fragmentation position. As drawn, the already barcoded long fragments become shorter end-tagged fragments through a second restriction digest. This preserves the depicted ordering without asserting that it is the reaction order of every ddRAD protocol.
operations.mechanism: Second restriction digestion is specified by the figure label. Enzyme identity, end chemistry, and the intended ddRAD protocol are not resolved by the supplied abstract-only application evidence.
operations.information_effect: The shown shorter fragments retain the first barcoded end. Restriction-site availability limits comparability of sampled loci: the supplied avian ddRAD abstract reports declining sharing of homologous loci with accumulating restriction-site polymorphisms.

operations.label: Add P2 adapter
operations.description: Adds the green terminal adapter to the opposite end of the depicted shorter, first-adapter-bearing genomic fragments, producing fragments with two different terminal interfaces. This is a shared schematic stage following either fragmentation label, not a pooling step.
operations.mechanism: For Baird RAD, ligation of a divergent Y-shaped P2 adapter introduces the reverse-amplification interface. That interface becomes primer-competent following forward extension from P1. This mechanism is not assigned to ddRAD or the Willing preparation without matching full-text evidence.
operations.information_effect: Adds the second amplification interface while preserving the barcode-to-genomic-insert association. In Baird RAD the P2 design makes productive amplification dependent on the first-adapter-bearing fragment class.

The reverse amplification primer is unable to bind to P2 unless the complementary sequence is filled in during the first round of forward elongation originating from the P1 amplification primer. The structure of this adapter ensures that only P1 adapter-ligated RAD tags will be amplified during the final PCR amplification step (Fig. 1D).

operations.label: Amplify
operations.description: Amplifies the two-interface genomic fragments to yield the final DNA library. Although the terminal image uses uncolored blue lines, Baird RAD identifies the enriched product as P1-bearing RAD tags.
operations.mechanism: For Baird RAD, PCR selectively enriches P1-bearing tags because forward extension from P1 fills the sequence needed for the reverse primer to bind at P2. Only broad amplification is supported for the other variants at figure scope.
operations.information_effect: Increases copies of the selected genomic fragments while preserving their sample-barcode association. Downstream sequencing measures restriction-site-flanking genomic sequence for SNP discovery/genotyping; it does not establish whole-genome completeness. Paired-end read data and their use for extended flanking contigs are supported by the Willing abstract, not by an extra drawn sequencing operation.

method_scopes.rationale: RAD-Seq is explicitly associated with Baird et al. in the card. Its full-text Figure 1 and RAD-marker-generation section support restriction digestion, P1 barcode addition, random shearing, divergent P2 addition, and selective PCR in this order. The second restriction digest is the labeled ddRAD alternative and is excluded from this route. The final library is a reduced representation of restriction-site-flanking genomic DNA used for SNP discovery and genotyping. Optional multiplex pooling is reported in Baird but is not a separate operation in the supplied Illumina diagram.

method_scopes.rationale: The title and catalogue description group paired-end RAD with the displayed shearing route; the card specifically cites Willing et al. for this member. Its available abstract confirms paired-end RAD-seq data used to assemble extended contigs flanking restriction sites and discover markers. Thus this is a distinct readout/assembly variant, not simply another spelling of single-end RAD or ddRAD. These operation IDs identify its family-level depiction only. The abstract does not verify the preparation order or whether Baird-specific P1/P2 selective-PCR chemistry was used in the Willing implementation; those details remain unassigned to this member.

method_scopes.rationale: ddRAD-Seq/ddRADseq names the explicitly labeled second-restriction-digest alternative, not the Shear operation. The graph retains its placement after first-adapter addition because that is what the diagram shows. The downstream adapter and amplification stages are preserved only at the grouped schematic level. The supplied DaCosta/Sorenson abstract is an application of double-digest RAD and documents marker-comparability limitations; it does not establish a preparation sequence or resolve which ddRAD implementation Illumina intended. No matched ddRAD protocol full text is supplied, so second-digest timing relative to ligation and variant-specific adapter chemistry remain unresolved. The two fragmentation routes are alternatives, not a claim of experimentally demonstrated interchangeability.

corrections.primary_statement: Baird Figure 1D identifies the amplified/enriched RAD product as tags that have P1; Figure 1A identifies P1 as carrying the barcode and primer interfaces. The Baird-specific library description therefore follows the primary evidence and treats omission of terminal colors as schematic simplification, rather than a biochemical loss of the adapters. This resolution is not used to assign the Baird Y mechanism to all variants.

unknowns.question: Which ddRAD implementation is intended, and does its second digest occur after first-adapter ligation as depicted? A matched protocol full text or figure identifying the digestion/ligation order and adapter interfaces is needed. The supplied avian application abstract does not resolve this. The uncertainty does not block extraction of the labeled schematic alternative.

Which preparation chemistry, if any, differs in the Willing paired-end implementation from the family shearing route, including its second-adapter and amplification design? The available abstract supports the paired-data/contig readout only; the matching full-text library-preparation description or figure would be needed to assign variant-specific chemistry. Family-level depiction remains interpretable.
